technical_and_design_decisions: For XD 1.0 to 1.1 migration (U1), backward compatibility for public custom module APIs will be maintained where possible, with automated migration scripts provided for common configuration changes to reduce user porting effort.
The Pig integration sample (U2) will target Pig 0.15 (the latest stable version supported by XD 1.1) and be packaged as a standalone sample project with clear execution instructions.

Windows build support (U3) will prioritize Windows Subsystem for Linux 2 (WSL 2) as the primary build environment to minimize platform-specific code changes, with native Windows build support documented for contributors without WSL access.

Windows acceptance tests (U4) will run on AWS EC2 Windows Server 2022 instances, with CI integration via GitHub Actions to enable automated test execution on every pull request to the open source repository.

Spark Streaming processors (U5) will be implemented as two separate modules: a Java-based module using lambdas for simple use cases, and a Scala-based module for advanced use cases, both adhering to XD's standard processor module contract.
The reference guide copyright update (U6) will be applied to the Asciidoctor source documentation file, with the PDF regenerated from source to ensure consistency across all output formats.

The Kafka SI GA upgrade (U7) will be performed on a dedicated feature branch, with backported changes from the XD Kafka module validated against the Kafka SI GA release candidate before merging to main.
The SHDP GA upgrade (U8) will use the latest GA release version, with full regression testing run to identify and resolve any compatibility issues with existing XD functionality.
assumptions: The developer has full access to the XD codebase, AWS EC2 console, and the project's CI/CD pipeline configuration.
All third-party dependencies (Pig 0.15, Kafka SI GA, SHDP GA) are compatible with XD 1.1's core runtime and the required Java 17+ runtime.
Existing XD acceptance test suites are platform-agnostic enough to run on Windows with only minor path and line-ending adjustments.
The project's reference guide is maintained in Asciidoctor source format in the project's documentation repository.
Custom modules built for XD 1.0 use only public, non-deprecated APIs that are retained in XD 1.1.
The developer has prior working knowledge of the XD codebase, Spring Framework, Apache Spark, Pig, Kafka, and SHDP to reduce learning curve effort.
